text.p: - To increase his popularity, President Boris Yeltsin desperately needs to win a battle, whether by sending help to Peru to defeat Marxist rebels or attacking tax dodgers at home.
- President Yeltsin urges quick and tough action against tax dodgers among alcohol distillers and dealers.
- The introduction of a new tax on border crossings will hurt Russians economically and could seriously dent Russia's reputation.
- President Yeltsin takes the problem of tax dodging on the alcohol market under his personal control.
- Rumours about a possible merger of Russian oil giants Sidanko, Sibneft and VNK send waves through the oil market.
- 1997 could become the year of the great European divide as NATO refuses to heed Russia's warning against eastwards expansion and says Moscow should change its attitude towards the alliance.
- Russian new long-haul carrier aircraft Tu-204 looks to Asian markets to take on big Western plane manufacturers.
- A proclaimed state monopoly on alcohol production cannot be implemented as such and will only mean stricter government control over production and distribution of strong spirits.
